today_theme:
• TARIFF CLOCK: Trump's July 4 EU deadline is the dominant macro risk event.
• YIELD WATCH: 10Y at 4.39%; breach of 4.50% could reset equity multiples.
• METALS SIGNAL: Gold, silver, copper surging — inflation/dollar debasement trade live.
• JOBS REPORT: April payrolls today determine Fed narrative for June meeting.
• AI ANCHOR: Tech rally record highs; breadth divergence is the hidden risk to watch.

catalysts.headline: Trump Threatens EU With 'Much Higher' Tariffs If No Deal By July 4
catalysts.analysis: President Trump issued a hard deadline of July 4 for the EU to finalize a trade agreement, threatening escalating tariffs if unmet. This injects fresh trade-war risk into global markets, pressuring European equities (DAX -0.71%, CAC -0.67%) and multinationals with EU exposure. Watch EUR/USD resilience and EU negotiator response; a breakdown in talks could reprice risk assets sharply lower.

catalysts.headline: April Jobs Report Due: Labor Market Cooling But Resilient
catalysts.analysis: Consensus expects a stable but softening labor market print, balancing Fed rate-cut hopes against lingering inflation concerns. A weak number could reignite rate-cut bets and lift equities; a hot number could push 10Y yields above 4.5% and pressure growth stocks. Watch the unemployment rate and wage growth as the two most Fed-sensitive variables.

catalysts.headline: AI Trade Fuels Record-Setting Rally in S&P 500 and Nasdaq
catalysts.analysis: Prior session saw Dow surge 600 points with S&P 500 and Nasdaq hitting records driven by AI sector momentum. This confirms the AI investment supercycle narrative remains the dominant equity driver, with tech leadership broadening. Watch semiconductor names and cloud infrastructure spending guidance for sustainability signals.

catalysts.headline: Gold Surges Past $4,728 as Silver and Copper Lead Metals Complex
catalysts.analysis: Gold +0.61%, Silver +1.82%, Copper +2.56% signal broad metals strength, suggesting inflation re-pricing and real-asset demand. The commodity surge alongside a weaker DXY (-0.30%) points to dollar debasement concerns and potential stagflation hedging. Watch whether copper's industrial signal aligns with global growth data or diverges as a pure liquidity play.

catalysts.headline: 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to 4.392%, Steepening the Curve
catalysts.analysis: The 10Y yield jumped +0.83% while the 3M T-Bill eased, steepening the curve and signaling bond market concern over fiscal deficits and inflation persistence. Rising long-end yields compress equity multiples, particularly for high-duration growth and tech names. Watch the 4.50% level on the 10Y as a potential inflection point for equity volatility.

trade_ideas.thesis: Rising 10Y yields at 4.39% and tariff escalation risk create headwinds for current elevated multiples; a failed breakout after record highs sets up a mean-reversion short. A jobs report surprise to the upside could accelerate the move lower as rate-cut hopes fade.

Gold is breaking out to new highs amid dollar weakness, tariff uncertainty, and fiscal deficit concerns — classic Dalio all-weather store-of-value conditions. Silver and copper confirming metals bull market adds macro validation.

AI capex cycle remains intact with hyperscalers reaffirming spending; NVDA is the picks-and-shovels play Lynch would identify as the dominant franchise in a secular growth theme. Strong earnings momentum and pricing power justify premium multiple.

daily_conclusion:
RESUMEN:
Markets are taking a modest breather after yesterday's record-setting AI-fueled rally, with all major U.S. indexes slightly in the red as rising bond yields and Trump's EU tariff threat inject caution into the session. The big story today is the April jobs report — a single data release that could either confirm the Fed's patience on rate cuts or force a rethink entirely.
LO MÁS IMPORTANTE:
• April Jobs Report — this is the Fed's most important input right now; a strong number pushes rate cuts further away and could lift yields, pressuring stocks.
• Trump's July 4 EU Tariff Deadline — a new trade war front with Europe creates uncertainty for multinational companies and global supply chains over the next two months.
• Gold and Metals Surging — gold at $4,728, silver and copper both rallying hard signals that smart money is hedging against inflation and dollar weakness simultaneously.
CONCEPTO DEL DÍA:
**Yield Curve Steepening** means that long-term interest rates (like the 10-year Treasury at 4.39%) are rising faster than short-term rates. Think of it like a bank charging you more for a 30-year mortgage than a 1-year loan — when that gap widens, it usually signals the market expects higher inflation or more government borrowing ahead, which can put pressure on stock valuations especially for growth companies.
PARA MAÑANA:
Digest today's jobs report carefully — the market reaction in the first hour after release will set the tone for the week's close and signal whether the "soft landing" narrative survives into the weekend. Over the next 48 hours, watch for any EU official response to Trump's July 4 tariff ultimatum, which could either calm or significantly escalate global trade anxiety.
